name: sol-advisor
description: Score-routed native workers with tier-specific preflight and a weekly savings receipt.

interface.longDescription: Activate Sol Advisor once for the current Codex chat. Primary GPT-5.6 Sol / High always resolves requirements, architecture, interfaces, ownership, acceptance criteria, and an exact implementation packet. It then scores only the remaining implementation: 1.0–2.9 uses native GPT-5.6 Luna / Max, 3.0–5.0 uses native GPT-5.6 Terra / Medium, 5.1–6.5 uses native GPT-5.6 Terra / High, 6.6–7.9 uses native GPT-5.6 Sol / Medium, and 8.0–10.0 uses a separate native GPT-5.6 Sol / High implementer. Activation authorizes the score-selected native worker without separate task or model authorization. Scored read-only and modifying work starts at its mapped tier. Availability is checked for the selected tier with fresh current-turn evidence; unrelated missing roles never block a healthy worker. An unavailable tier moves upward in order through Luna Max, Terra Medium, Terra High, Sol Medium, and Sol High implementer; primary Sol High executes as the terminal fallback. Every worker title starts with its spelled-out model and effort. Primary Sol / High verifies every result, and modifying native implementations receive a fresh Sol / High review before acceptance. Completed tasks end with two model lines plus a compact three-line weekly usage and routing-savings receipt; a fallback includes its verified reason. Direct ON/OFF markers preserve state only inside the current chat. Minimum-sufficient, token, and time checkpoints shape scope without overriding the numeric implementation band unless a lane is unavailable or incapable. Worker interruptions force fresh primary routing. The first activation each local day audits DannyMac180/sol-advisor without automatic merges. Accepted fork changes finish on jessejaffe/sol-advisor main.
defaultPrompt: Tell me “Turn Sol Advisor on” in this chat when you want Sol-led routing; otherwise it stays off.
